reviewers: two independent AI reviewer agents per language (slots A: README-first sampling, B: code-first request-path sampling), model claude-opus-5-5, read-only, no execution; same rubric (docs/methodology/code-quality-rubric.md)
caveats: AI reviewers, not humans: scores are subjective judgements, never facts
ceiling/compression: almost all scores are 4-5, so the rubric discriminates little between engines
reviewers knew the language (no blinding possible)
extensibility (rubric item 5) is not scored here; it is measured by the change-task costs (report 7)

kernel_cohort.note: assembly native-kernel libraries (kernel cohort, ADR-0016); reviewed after the kernel-optimize merge. Not comparable with and never ranked against the engine scores: a 20-kernel library is a different artefact from a complete engine. Same reviewer slots (A README-first, B code-first from the ABI header and dispatcher), rubric items interpreted for a kernel library (ABI, bounds/tails, exactness; testability includes the library's own verification aids).
observations: Task texts for the two optimize runs differ only in the hardware notes; the AArch64 agent nevertheless kept its guard-page harness, mutation checks and clobber audit out of the repository ('only assembly belongs in the repo'), while the x86-64 agent committed them under verify/. Both ARM reviewers scored testability 3 for this reason.

No functional defect found by any reviewer; suspected issues are design notes (index over-stores within the documented capacity, group_sum EINVAL undo pass assumes no aliasing, a 7th-argument stack read in count kernels), hardening gaps (no BTI/GNU property note on AArch64) and stale documentation (README module-map line counts, an SVE header claiming emulation-only validation).
